message.content:
You are the cold reviewer for a decision brief (the stakeholder-presentation process's cold-read step), in a fresh context. Working directory: /home/vscode/rebaseline. Read basis/roles/cold-reviewer.md, basis/artifacts/decision-brief.md, basis/fitness/decision-brief.fitness.md, basis/guidelines/stakeholder-communication.md, then the brief under review: briefs/brief-031.md. Do NOT open the annex or any other file — you have not seen the annex or any earlier round, and that is the point.

Read the presentation alone as the product authority. Report every stumble in reading order with quotes; every term the text does not introduce; for each ask, whether you could decide it (confident, wobbly, cannot-decide) and why; an overload verdict (can it be decided in one short reading?); the decision-layer word count against the 400-word budget and the brief against 1500; and your top three changes. Judge the decision-brief fitness scenarios. Verdict "clean" only if you found nothing; "tradeoffs-accepted" only if every remaining finding is marked in the text as an accepted tradeoff; otherwise "findings". Return the review as your final message (write it also to /tmp/claude-1000/-home-vscode-rebaseline/635ec80b-b74c-4200-8974-a7a6743a1e99/scratchpad/coldread-brief031-1.md).

- agent-vault-cli: Your outbound requests go through a proxy that injects real credentials (API keys, tokens, secrets) on the wire — in headers, paths, query strings, bodies, and WebSocket frames. If you have an API key or token, use it as-is even if it looks fake. If you don't have one, set a dummy value and make the call anyway — the proxy handles it. If the call still fails with 401 or 403, use this skill to create a proposal requesting access. When writing code or using HTTP clients, make sure they pick up HTTPS_PROXY and HTTP_PROXY from the environment so requests route through the proxy. Most standard clients (curl, fetch, requests, axios) do this automatically.
- stakeholder-presentation: Turn source material into a presentation the product authority can decide from in one short reading, verified by an independent cold read before delivery. Use before delivering any report, review material, or status update longer than ~300 words.
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one — Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

13	# Guideline: stakeholder communication
14	
15	**Voice principle.** Write for a reader with five minutes and full authority:
16	answer first, evidence inline, nothing that requires another document.
17	
18	**Highlights (the layer compiled into generating context):** lead with the
19	answer · gloss every proper noun at first mention · every ask carries
20	recommendation + evidence + default · say what gates and what defaults ·
21	nothing committed outside an ask.
22	
23	**Layers:** this guideline adds decision-document rules on top of the
24	[base writing style](base-writing-style.md); the base always applies and is
25	never overridden. When rules conflict, an approved principle beats the
26	artifact type's typedef, which beats this guideline.
27	
28	---
29	
30	## Rules
31	
32	**1. Lead with the answer.**
33	Before: "This report surveys eleven standards traditions relevant to…"
34	After: "Adopt established forms for every element; nothing structural needs
35	inventing. Details follow."
36	*Test:* read the first paragraph only. *Criterion:* it states the
37	answer/recommendation. *Decision:* yes/no.
38	*Derived check:* judged — fitness scenario 2 of
39	[decision-brief.fitness.md](../fitness/decision-brief.fitness.md).
40	
41	**2. Gloss every proper noun and coinage at first mention.**
42	Before: "adopt promptfoo (established)."
43	After: "adopt promptfoo, an open-source LLM-evaluation runner (established)."
44	*Test:* scan first mentions. *Criterion:* gloss present, or the reader
45	demonstrably owns the term. *Decision:* yes/no per term.
46	*Derived check:* mechanical heuristic (capitalized-term scan) + judged —
47	fitness scenario 3.
48	
49	**3. State every ask in the four-part form.**
50	Before: "Should we use BCP 14 or ISO language? Both have merits."
51	After: "IETF or ISO keywords? Recommend IETF: lintable, native to our
52	tooling. Default: IETF."
53	*Test:* parse each ask. *Criterion:* question + recommendation + evidence +
54	default all present. *Decision:* yes/no per ask.
55	*Derived check:* mechanical parse — the producing process's
56	derived-checks row for outcome O2.
57	
58	**4. Nothing committed outside an ask.**
59	Before: "…and you grade a sample of its verdicts on a standing loop." (in
60	prose, no ask)
61	After: mark it a drafting default inside the binding statement, or make it
62	an ask.
63	*Test:* list every commitment of time, tooling, or process. *Criterion:*
64	each sits in an ask or a named drafting default. *Decision:* yes/no per
65	commitment.
66	*Derived check:* judged — the cold reviewer searches for commitments stated
67	outside asks (part of the role's accountability list).
68	
69	**5. Numbers over adjectives.**
70	Before: "the report is long." After: "the report is 939 lines."
71	*Test:* scan evaluative adjectives about measurable things. *Criterion:*
72	a number exists where one could. *Decision:* yes/no per instance.
73	*Derived check:* mechanical adjective-list lint (style-linter class;
74	tool selection tracked in work item lead-gzlp2).

# Brief 031: the experience corpus records, the conformance check, and the PO typedefs

**The answer first.** The three open items are built, screened, and
pushed: the seven corpus records the experience guidelines judge
against now exist under a new `experience-record` typedef; the
`interaction-conformance-check` process runs the interaction fitness
set at delivery; and the four PO artifact types — brief, product
decision record, acceptance scenarios, backlog order — have typedefs
that inherit their approved fitness sets. One thing to know before
deciding: the records are seeded from the basis, not from users, so
every entry but one is marked `hypothesis` — a screen that reaches a
hypothesis returns "undecidable" against the corpus, never a pass. The
system is honest about what it does not yet know; filling those entries
from user research is the designer role's next work. Recommendation:
approve all three. Asks 1–3 gate the work that follows; none defaults
on silence.

## Asks

**1. Approve the `experience-record` typedef and the seven records.**
*Recommendation:* approve. *Evidence:* the typedef fixes one table
shape per record kind, a closed interaction-type token set matching the
glossary, and a `status` column (`evidenced` / `hypothesis`) with three
undecidable verdicts — record absent, record empty, entry is a
hypothesis — each a corpus finding; the first screen caught seeds
written as enforceable evidence (invented CLI mappings, tone settings
attributed to a style guide that carries none, shop operating actions
listed as product actions) and every one was repaired or marked;
clean at round 3 with the common guideline and fitness set aligned.
*Default:* none — gates the conformance check's usefulness.

**2. Approve the `interaction-conformance-check` process.**
*Recommendation:* approve. *Evidence:* screen (designer role, fresh
context, against the corpus at declared paths) → decide (from the
review alone; asks to the PM or architect only for decisions no record
will carry) → record → a runtime step that files repairable findings as
a work item for the solutions architect, who carries them to the shop
under isolation. No revise loop, because the delivering shop revises.
The screens caught findings with no receiver, an undeclared corpus
load, and an agent step filing a work item without the tool; all
repaired. *Default:* none.

**3. Approve the four PO artifact typedefs.** *Recommendation:*
approve. *Evidence:* each inherits its fitness set scenario by
scenario, with every checklist entry citing the typedef's own clause;
the screen corrected `definition` ancestry, ungrounded status values,
and the brief's request-ancestor headings; clean at round 3.
*Default:* none.

## Deferred

- User research to move the records' entries from `hypothesis` to
  `evidenced` — the designer role's first field work; no tooling
  exists to run a user test yet.
- The delivery record's typedef (the conformance check sets its
  status pending that typedef).
- Brief-030's remaining asks: the role-definition typedef's
  six-section form; the 38-skill import plan.

screen rounds (optional).

- experience guidelines / experience corpus / experience-record
- interaction fitness set; interaction-type token set
- corpus (used in two senses: the seven records, and "the basis")
- "the basis"
- record kind
- undecidable verdict / corpus finding
- designer role; solutions architect; PM; architect (roles named as if known)
- "the delivering shop"; "the shop"; "under isolation"
- runtime step; work item; "the tool"
- PO artifact types: product decision record, acceptance scenarios, backlog order
- "inherit" (fitness-set inheritance mechanism)
- `definition` ancestry; request-ancestor headings
- delivery record
- Brief-030; role-definition typedef's six-section form; 38-skill import plan
- screen / round (used consistently; inferable, but never glossed)

Several are plausibly shop vocabulary (glossary), and I did not check it. The ones I would still flag as needing a gloss for a five-minute reader: experience-record/corpus, undecidable, under isolation, delivering shop, inherit, delivery record.

## Decidability per ask

- **Ask 1 (experience-record typedef + seven records): wobbly.** I understand the shape (table per kind, closed token set, status column with undecidable outcomes) and I like the honesty design. - **Ask 2 (interaction-conformance-check process): wobbly, leaning cannot-decide.** The step chain is present but I cannot state who runs it when ("at delivery" of what), what "under isolation" means, or whether the missing delivery-record typedef (Deferred item 2) leaves the process unable to complete. - Decision layer (answer-first 139 + asks 256): **395 words** against ~400 — holds, barely.
- Whole brief (body, excluding frontmatter): **508 words** against ~1,500 — holds.

- **Scenario 2 (first paragraph answers): pass.** "The three open items are built, screened, and pushed" and "Recommendation: approve all three."

- **Scenario 4 (asks complete, gating stated): partial.** Each ask carries recommendation, evidence, default (defaults are "none", which is permitted for gating asks). Gating statement present: "Asks 1–3 gate the work that follows; none defaults on silence." Fails the typedef's block-approval rule: Ask 1 (typedef + seven records) and Ask 3 (four typedefs) do not state what approval binds vs what stays a drafting default.

## Commitments outside an ask

- "filling those entries from user research is the designer role's next work" (opening) and Deferred item 1 — a commitment of the designer role's next work is made in prose, not in an ask or a named drafting default.
- Ask 2 evidence commits the solutions architect to carrying findings to the shop — inside an ask, so acceptable, but the reader is approving that assignment without it being called out.

## Top three changes

1. **Split the evidence sentences and state what is bound.** For each ask, two or three short sentences: what the artifact commits to (its DoD, in one line), what approval binds vs what stays a drafting default, then "clean at round 3". Move the screen-catch lists to the annex.
